# Review Agent

Self-hosted, advisory pull-request review with bounded model tools, deterministic authorization, PostgreSQL state, and GitHub App publication.

Release state: v0.5.0-rc.1
License: EUPL-1.2 (Version 1.2 only). Third-party components retain their original licenses.
Authentication: GitHub App only; approve each installation once, then organization-managed repositories activate on their first signed `/review` delivery without a per-repository deployment command. Requester authorization still gates the review. Explicit per-repository activation remains available.
Model policy: set REVIEW_AGENT_MODEL_PROVIDER, REVIEW_AGENT_MODEL, and REVIEW_AGENT_REASONING_EFFORT; the supported providers are openai-codex and anthropic; the documented default uses Codex device-code OAuth.
Behavior ownership: one environment normally uses the neutral `default-standard` profile for every approved organization and repository. GitHub App installation controls access, not behavior. A repository may add an optional `.review-agent/` package; use another deployment profile only for a different shared identity or fixed review policy.
Trigger: a user with current GitHub write/admin permission, or a per-repository additional-user grant in the console's Who can request reviews list, posts a new top-level `/review` or `/review docs` comment on an open same-repository pull request. Console grants follow stable GitHub account IDs and do not change GitHub permissions. Feedback still requires GitHub write/admin permission.
Security boundary: the model has no shell, merge authority, App private key, installation token, or arbitrary GitHub write access.
Feedback: an authorized command is accepted whether or not the published review shows the command help (`REVIEW_AGENT_FEEDBACK_ENABLED`). `/review false-positive` suppresses the same finding while its code context is unchanged and the decision has not expired (180 days); `/review intentional` also requires the same accepted ADR metadata in the current base snapshot. `/review feedback scope` and `/review feedback missed` record evidence for gated improvement without silently changing live behavior.
Repository guidance: repositories may opt into `.review-agent/config.toml`, one optional `instructions.md`, explicitly ordered `context/**/*.md`, and typed ADRs under `.review-agent/decisions/`; all are read from the exact pull-request base commit and cannot weaken the deployment safety contract.

## Coding-agent handoff

If no source checkout was provided, clone this repository and check out the exact runtime release named above. Then use the versioned repository-local `skills/install-review-agent/SKILL.md`; Codex and Claude Code mirrors are included, so do not install a floating global copy. Read only the platform-relevant documents above, prepare and validate the non-secret installation plan, and stop only for owner approvals, protected secret placement, DNS, model login, deployment approval, and the first live `/review`. On Dokploy, use Deploy when the source revision changes and verify the completed deployment commit. Finish with doctor, inventory, dry-run, and live-review evidence; report unknowns instead of guessing.

## Repository-only handoff

When Review Agent is already deployed and the target repository is covered by an approved installation, use the same versioned installation skill and its `Configure one repository` section. This mode configures guidance; it does not install or activate Review Agent. Do not change the deployment, GitHub App, model, or secrets. Prepare the environment that the skill documents. Copy `examples/repository-context/.review-agent` only when the target has no `.review-agent/` directory; otherwise preserve the existing package and edit it in place. Keep technical context explicitly ordered in `config.toml`, store indexed ADRs under `.review-agent/decisions/`, and validate the repository with the command that section gives. Submit the package through normal repository review; it becomes active only after merge when a later pull request reads it from the base commit.

## Operator interface

Source checkout: how the checkout is installed and how its operator command is called differ between releases, so take both from the install skill of the release you checked out, not from this page. That skill prepares the environment, reports the shipped capabilities, runs the preflight, and validates an optional repository package; the validation is offline and prints hashes, paths, and status rather than file bodies. After deployment, run `review-agent-admin doctor`, inventory, activation, and `smoke-test --dry-run` inside the documented service container. These commands return bounded JSON except where the command documents another default.

Quality reporting: run `review-agent-memory quality --days 30` globally or add `--repo owner/repository`. It reports explicit signals beside their denominators and keeps the current triage backlog visible. A missed issue requires explicit operator triage; a coding agent must not choose the status or target owner.
